claims.text: The Arc de Triomphe sits proudly at the centre of a massive intersection where twelve different radiating avenues meet to form a star shape.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was originally commissioned by Napoleon in 1806 as a grand tribute to his victories and the soldiers who fought for France.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Its original architect, Jean-François Chalgrin, was heavily inspired by the ancient Roman Arch of Titus when designing it.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unfortunately, Napoleon did not live to see it finished, as the massive monument was not actually completed until 1836, long after his death.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The inner and outer surfaces of the arch are intricately engraved with the names of famous French military victories and generals.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Directly beneath the vault lies the deeply moving Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, which is marked by a continuously burning eternal flame.
claims.subject: self
